A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ParallaxRAG work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original retrieval and QA experiments, BioASQ transfer results, component ablations, and attention-head analyses, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds controlled interventions, comparison results, verification checks, repeated-run statistics, and latency measurements.

M1.justification: The aligned multi-head representations, PSR-enhanced distance encoding, shared MLP scoring, query-aware gating, shortest-path supervision, and generation procedure are retained. Sections 3.1–3.2 disclose head extraction, projection, and scorer inputs more explicitly without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate WebQSP and CWQ, cross-dataset transfer, and CWQ-to-BioASQ transfer covering Yes/No, Factoid, and List questions. The additional controls and analyses remain within this coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds RoG + GraphRAG-FI and REL-RAG + GPT-4o-mini. The BioASQ comparison adds Qwen3-Plus alone and Single-View + Qwen3-Plus, providing previously absent comparisons using the same generator. SubgraphRAG's added GPT-4o suffix identifies a retained row with unchanged scores.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include removing heads 8, 9, and 12, shuffling head-to-query-view assignments, combining these interventions, and matching generator, prompt, and context budget in BioASQ controls. V3 also adds comparisons across extraction models, inspection of a random 10% subset, and per-stage latency measurement. Figure 4 relabels CWQ as CWQ-sub, without defining the subset or establishing a rerun; the main training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds controlled head-disruption experiments testing functional specialization, extends the existing no-PSR ablation to retrieval metrics, and adds BioASQ controls isolating retrieval design. Extraction-stability checks and latency decomposition add further analyses. The earlier sensitivity study, alternative-encoder analyses, probing/DDD experiments, and three case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Beyond the retained DDD confidence interval and p-value, v3 newly reports five independent training runs with means and standard deviations in Table 7, paired-bootstrap tests against SubgraphRAG and GNN-RAG, and variability for extraction and latency. V2 does not specify a comparable training-run count, so an increase in runs cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: For the retained GPT-4o/200-triple configuration, Table 2 changes WebQSP Macro-F1/Hit from 77.82/93.63 to 78.80/93.53 and CWQ from 61.22/67.72 to 62.31/70.74. Probe accuracy changes from 46.5% to 52.3%. Substantial new comparator, intervention, BioASQ-control, stability, and latency results are added; the original main retrieval and component-ablation scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The PSR/DE derivations, weighted listwise objective, reasoning-step and head-metric definitions, and DDD formulation retain their mathematical substance. The added scorer equation explicates the existing shared-MLP component; equation numbering and the H-to-F notation change introduce no new theoretical argument or formal property.

C1.justification: The headline contributions remain aligned multi-head KG retrieval, hop-dependent head specialization, state-of-the-art retrieval/QA, reduced hallucination, and zero-shot transfer. The new conclusion consolidates these claims rather than redefining their scope.

C2.justification: V3 adds a shortest-path-supervision bias limitation and interpretations concerning generator capacity, retrieval precision, and component importance. DDD conclusions become more cautious functional evidence. The unchanged shallow-query failure is reframed as unnecessary but factually correct context inducing conservative generation. Appendix D.2 also introduces a generation-dominated runtime interpretation that conflicts with its latency tables.

D1.justification: V3 documents head slicing, shared projection, augmented entity features, MLP inputs, and the triple-verification prompt and matching procedure. The implementation link changes from anonymous hosting to a named GitHub repository. Conversely, Appendix B.3 abbreviates v2's fuller QA demonstration with ellipses, reducing that documentation; the principal optimizer and generation hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: Related Work substantially expands direct contrasts with GNN-RAG, SubgraphRAG, MRAG, and path-based or reinforcement-learning approaches. New citations include attention-specialization studies, RoE, Deep GraphRAG, REL-RAG, and dataset references. Existing cited works are retained, while the positioning around aligned hop-specific representations becomes more explicit.

P1.justification: Related Work and several results, limitations, and case-interpretation passages are substantially rewritten. V3 expands method explanations, adds a conclusion and acknowledgments, and reorganizes appendix material around verification and additional results. It also introduces unresolved citation markers and awkward equation cross-references.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 are substantially redrawn, with Figure 1 moved to the first page. Comparison tables are expanded or regrouped, and new disruption, stability, and latency tables are added. The former full-page QA prompt figure becomes a shorter boxed template. Existing sensitivity, encoder, and case-study figures are largely retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: V3's head interventions and matched-generator BioASQ controls strengthen attribution to multi-view retrieval, while verification details and uncertainty reporting improve assessability. The net gain is limited by reduced QA-prompt detail and inconsistencies in new reporting. In particular, Tables 8–9 report retrieval taking 38.78/82.35 seconds versus generation taking 3.124/3.784 seconds, although Appendix D.2 says generation dominates. These issues prevent treating the expanded evidence as a substantial overall quality improvement.
